question: Wei had 162 minutes of video-call credit, or two hours and forty-two minutes as his phone app displayed it, more than his roommate Tom's 15 minutes. He split the credit evenly across six family group chats, and this story follows only one of those chats from here. That chat then received a 26-minute bonus from a promotion. A loyalty reward multiplied the chat's remaining minutes sevenfold. Finally, 243 minutes were used up during a long weekend of calls. How many minutes were left in that chat?

In the morning the nursery's mint trays each held 74 plants, and Kit pricked out 51 more plants into each tray, filling 5 trays that made up the whole stock. In the afternoon 292 plants were sold at the plant fair. In the evening Kit divided every plant left in the stock into 6 rooted cuttings, each potted up as a new plant, and a neighbour dropped off 15 potted mint plants for the stock. How many mint plants are in the stock now?

In the morning, a courier named Wes had 119 packages loaded in his van. By midday he picked up 48 more packages from the depot. That afternoon he delivered 119 packages to a large office building. In the evening he picked up 63 more packages for a late round. Right before his shift ended, he handed off 29 packages to another driver during a stop that lasted half an hour, or 30 minutes. How many packages did Wes have in his van after handing off packages to the other driver?

A division starts with 138 units. It divides by 3 (46). It multiplies by 3 (138). It loses 34 (104). It loses 69 (35). Time from minutes to hours. One distractor: they had 55 overages. How many remain?
A warehouse had 170 boxes. They multiplied by 2. They added 76. They divided by 4. They multiplied by 8. They removed 601. How many boxes?

A contractor began with 228 labor hours. He subtracted 95 hours for administrative work. He added 22 hours from overtime. He multiplied by 5 for crew size calculation. He multiplied by 8 for daily output hours. He subtracted 2600 hours for subcontractor delegation. He multiplied by 8 for weekly planning (measured in weekly output hours). Throughout the week, morning site meetings, afternoon construction, and evening planning tracked weekly hours. Ten hours were allocated for training separately. What was the weekly output hour plan?

An amount was 68. By morning, it octupled (multiplied by 8). By midday, 48 were added. By afternoon, 557 were removed. By late afternoon, 70 arrived. By evening, it doubled. His colleague had 95. A distractor: a related amount was 110. How many final?

In the morning, a blood donation center had 164 pints collected, equal to about 20.5 gallons as the coordinator noted. By midday, another 15 pints came in from a company blood drive. In the afternoon, a local college donated 45 more pints. By evening, a hospital partnership added 40 pints. Late that night, a final mobile unit brought in 77 more pints. How many pints had the center collected by the end of the night?

A sales manager tracked revenue. Starting with 151 dollars, annual projection multiplied by 6 (906 dollars). Major expenses reduced 290 (616 dollars). Q1 bonus added 39 (655 dollars). Q2 performance added 77 (732 dollars). Q3-Q4 projections added 70 more. Converting to profit, this would represent quarterly earnings. A competitor made 200 dollars that quarter. How much in total?

A team started with 20 members. They multiplied by 4 to 80. They expanded 4 times to 320. They removed 189, leaving 131. They tripled to 393 members. His department has 100 members (separate). How many members total?

Each morning the Verano bakery loads 141 pastries onto every one of its 6 delivery trays. The bakery does this on each of the 5 mornings it opens. During the afternoons of that same week it added 35 pastries from a cancelled order and 53 more brought back from a market stall. The owner keeps a dozen recipe cards pinned above the oven. The van driver logs his rounds in minutes, although the delivery contract is written in hours. Each of the 6 branches in the chain then produced a week exactly like that one, and the whole chain's pastries were counted together. How many pastries were counted in total?
A factory had 119 units. They multiplied by 9. They multiplied by 6. They added 21 more. They removed 5558. His coworker manages 100 units separately. How many units?

Willa's bakery makes 3 batches of cookies every working day, with 177 cookies in each batch, and then adds a single extra batch of 44 cookies for the staff room. That daily total is more cookies than Xena's bakery across the street manages in a whole week. Willa's bakery works 3 days each week and keeps to the same daily output every working day. The current contract with the supermarket runs for 8 weeks. How many cookies will Willa's bakery make over the contract?

In the morning a crate of 132 oranges was divided equally into 3 baskets, one for each of the market's 3 fruit stalls, and Ben's stall received its basket. Later in the morning Ben added 33 oranges from his own garden to his stall. In the afternoon Ben sold 76 oranges to customers. In the evening a farmer dropped off 73 more oranges at Ben's stall. How many oranges does Ben's stall have now?

A florist began with 73 flowers. She multiplied by 4 through arrangements. She added 36 flowers from new deliveries. She added 60 more flowers. She added 3 bonus flowers. She multiplied by 7 for wedding bouquet quantity. She multiplied by 7 again for the season's total arrangements. Throughout the season, morning orders, afternoon arrangements, and evening prep measured in total seasonal arrangements. Her assistant arranged 8 additional bouquets. What was the season's total arrangement count?

A store started with 82 items on the shelf Monday. They multiplied by 8 through afternoon stocking. They multiplied by 2 for evening expansion. They multiplied by 3 for comprehensive inventory. They divided by 3 for quality sorting. The manager worked 8-hour shifts. How many items passed quality check?

A factory had 169 products. They multiplied by 6 for packaging cost. They removed 929 dollars in expenses. They multiplied by 4 for quarterly planning. They added 42 units from bonus production. They multiplied by 7 for the half-year calculation. They multiplied by 9 for annual projection. How many was the annual projection?

In the morning Amir picked 150 apples and divided them equally into 3 baskets, keeping 1 basket for himself. His sister Bela had 6 times as many apples in her cart as Amir had in his basket. In the afternoon Bela sold every apple in her cart for 7 cents each. In the evening she found 46 more cents in her apron pocket and added them to her takings. How many cents did Bela have in the evening?

In the morning Rob picked 20 plums from the garden tree, and his sister Sue picked 2 times as many plums as Rob did, so Sue's basket was fuller. Sue split her plums equally into 2 bags and gave 1 bag to their grandmother. In the afternoon Sue picked 58 more plums. In the evening she divided all the plums she had equally into 3 jars for jam, and then used 18 plums from the first jar for a pie. How many plums are left in the first jar?

In the morning, a factory had 27 units. Production increased 6 times by midday. By afternoon, 17 units were added. By evening, 36 units were added. A competitor produced 80 units. Their output then increased 5 times. How many units were produced?

A logistics company had 201 shipments. They multiplied by 7 for weekly tracking. Then by 8 for a full network. They divided by 4 to allocate to regions. They multiplied by 4 for multi-day tracking. Finally, they doubled the count for a two-week projection. One warehouse had extra shipments, but those were excluded from this count. How many shipments does the network track?
A warehouse had 175 boxes. They multiplied by 7. They multiplied by 3. They removed 2309. They removed 25. About 100 boxes are in transit, which is separate. How many boxes?

In the morning a soup kitchen served 67 bowls of soup, and then 35 more bowls as people kept arriving. At noon it ran a second sitting that served exactly as many bowls as the morning, making 2 sittings of the same size. In the afternoon 42 late arrivals were served, and in the evening another 66 people came for a bowl. The kitchen served exactly this number of bowls every day for 7 days. How many bowls of soup did it serve in total?

Amelia had 170 beads in her jewelry box, while her friend Zara had 90 beads in hers. Amelia used 55 beads to make a bracelet for her mom. She then bought 21 more beads at the craft store. A friend gave her 18 more beads for her birthday. Finally, she used 148 beads to make a large necklace for a craft fair. How many beads did Amelia have left after making the necklace?

Hh and Ii manage resources. In the morning, start with 200. By afternoon, they add 45 (245). By evening, add 75 (320). By closing, add 9 (329). By night, 212 are used (117). Morning and evening emphasized. How many remain?
